Trail_Kit_Decision__c.Guidance__c: Name two or three people rather than a whole profile. A small pilot you can ask questions of beats a broad rollout nobody owns.

Trail_Kit_Decision__c.Question__c: What syncs — email, calendar, or both?
Trail_Kit_Decision__c.Guidance__c: Email on, calendar off is the common starting answer. Calendar sync surfaces personal appointments people did not expect to share.

Trail_Kit_Decision__c.Question__c: How will you know it worked?
Trail_Kit_Decision__c.Guidance__c: Pick one record you will check, and one colleague who will confirm they see what you see.

Trail_Kit_Issue__c.Symptom__c: Nothing appears on any record after activating
Trail_Kit_Issue__c.Likely_Cause__c: The email connection did not complete, or sync has not run yet
Trail_Kit_Issue__c.Fix__c: Check for a Connected status first. If connected, wait — first sync can take hours.

Trail_Kit_Issue__c.Symptom__c: Consent screen is blocked or greyed out
Trail_Kit_Issue__c.Likely_Cause__c: Your email administrator has not granted the app permission
Trail_Kit_Issue__c.Fix__c: This needs whoever administers Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace. It is not a Salesforce permission.
Turn calendar sync off on the configuration, then tell the affected people what you changed.

_sections._comment: Standard page inventory every Trail Kit ships with. Editions may add pages (the learner edition adds an action plan, note pages and a programs placemat) but must not drop any of these.

_inserts._comment: Shared one-pagers that ship inside multiple kits. Authored once under templates/, never duplicated or edited per kit. Update one file and every kit reprints correctly.
_inserts.order: Bind in this order behind the tabs: Permitted Use, Glossary, Navigating Setup, Dev Org Setup, Where to Practice, Change Record.
_inserts.dev-org-setup: Dev Org Setup — Create a free Salesforce Developer org, with its real limitations.
_inserts.where-to-practice: Where to Practice — Developer org vs sandbox vs production, and how to choose. Pairs with the dev-org sheet and covers the case where a feature is absent on Developer Edition.
_inserts.setup-navigation: Navigating Setup — Find Setup, use Quick Find, tell Lightning from Classic, read Object Manager.
_inserts.glossary: Salesforce Glossary — Twenty terms every kit uses without defining. Written for someone who inherited an org.
_inserts.change-record: Change Record — Fill-in sheet: what changed, why, who approved, how to reverse. One per change.
_inserts.license: Permitted Use — License terms. Two variants via the edition prop: individual (learner) and organization-wide (nonprofit, after verification).
_inserts.sandboxes: The four sandbox types and their constraints. Reference rather than build-along, since Developer Edition orgs have no sandbox.
_inserts.security-model: What you can do versus what you can see, and which of the five things to reach for.
_inserts.report-types: What a report type decides before anyone opens the builder, and why good ones are what stop people exporting to spreadsheets.

_companion._comment: Every Trail Kit is a Product2 with a companion set of content that has to exist before it can go on sale. The PDF is one deliverable among several — a kit is not shippable until every required companion asset exists and is linked to the product record.

items.note: QR destinations now resolve from Product2 fields (see _qr_destinations). The fields exist in the model; the values are not yet entered for kit 01 or kit 02. Placeholder URLs currently sit in the templates and must be replaced by generation from the record before print.

_qr_destinations._comment: Every QR in a kit resolves from a field on the Product2 record for that kit, not from a URL typed into the template. Generation reads the record; nothing is hardcoded. A blank field is a blocked launch, not a broken link.

fields.feeds: Test data QR — the kit’s Google Drive folder
Kit page QR on the back cover
Referral block on the back cover — the buyer’s personal link

_qr_destinations.rule: Assembly fails rather than ships if a required URL field is blank on the product record. External destinations we do not own (Salesforce help, credential pages) are the exception and stay literal in the template.
